title: Seed growing secretly (Mark 4:26–34)
hookLine: the farmer sleeps and the seed grows, he knows not how

lines: A BEAN IN A PAPER CUP.
A FARMER WHO GOES TO BED.
cards: A bean in a paper cup, on a classroom windowsill. A kid waters it, then checks it. Every hour.
Sometimes the kid digs it up to see if anything is happening, and that's the end of the bean.
Grown-ups do a version of it too: checking the email, the scale, the savings, the person they're worried about, the prayer that hasn't been answered. Poking at the soil.
Today Jesus tells a very short story about a farmer who does the opposite. He plants, and then he goes to bed.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: "So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground; And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how."
The farmer isn't lazy. He did his part: he planted. But the growing isn't his job, and he doesn't understand it anyway.
Then a wonderful little word: "For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself."
Of herself, in Greek, is automate: on its own, without help.

teach.h: BLADE, THEN EAR, THEN FULL CORN.
teach.b: And it happens in order: "first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear." A green shoot, then a head of grain, then the full grain in the head.
You can't skip to the end, and pulling on the blade won't speed it up. Only at harvest does the farmer act again, and then fast, with the sickle.

teach.h: THE MUSTARD SEED, SIDE BY SIDE.
teach.b: Right after, Mark sets the mustard seed, which you met in Matthew on day twenty-four: the smallest seed, grown into a plant big enough for birds to nest in its shade.

Two seed stories side by side, both about what grows beyond what we can see or control. Christian readers hear them as pictures of God's kingdom: it grows quietly, often unseen, and the growing belongs to God.
Some also hear patience and trust in ordinary life. You plant. You sleep.
Something happens you don't understand. And Mark ends the chapter's teaching by saying Jesus told stories like these as people were able to hear them.

how: Christians often turn to this parable when their efforts seem to show no results, trusting that God gives the growth, and some churches keep old customs of blessing seeds and fields at planting time.

games.q: you're the farmer. the seed is in the ground and nothing shows yet. what do you do?
o: dig it up to check on it.
sleep and rise, night and day.
games.why: he sleeps and rises, and the seed springs up, he knoweth not how. he only acts again at harvest.

practice: Think of something you've planted and keep poking at: a project, a friendship you're trying to mend, a habit you've started, a hope.

Picture it as a seed in the dark soil, doing things you can't see, and picture yourself going to bed and leaving it there. If you pray, you can hand it to God for the night; if not, just let the soil hold it.

wordCard.voice: Automate, Greek for of itself: how Mark says the earth bears fruit on its own, while the farmer sleeps and knows not how.

orig.note: Greek: of itself, on its own. The earth bears fruit without the farmer's help.

carryVoice: Your line: it grows while you sleep. The growing was never the farmer's job. That's one hundred seventy-four days.
